turns.text: Why did researchers need C4.5, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

ID3 demonstrated entropy-based tree induction but had practical limits with continuous values, missing data, and overgrown trees. C4.5 extended the method into a more complete and deployable learning system.

C4.5 uses gain ratio, handles continuous and missing attributes, and prunes branches after training to improve generalization. It can also convert a learned tree into a compact set of classification rules.

Experts generally regard C4.5 as one of the most influential practical decision-tree systems. Its handling of data imperfections and pruning shaped later industrial tree implementations and interpretability practice.
